import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_2.csv"

df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_24_1: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_24_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_24_1 and Source3_24_2 on "movie_id"
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source1, df_source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by = [Source3_24_1.title], aggregations = 
# [avg(Source3_24_2.rating) grouped by gender F, avg(Source3_24_2.rating) grouped by gender M]

# To get gender, we need to join with Source3_24_0 (user info)
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_0.csv"
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_24_0: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']

# Join df_joined with df_source0 on user_id to get gender info
df_full = pd.merge(df_joined, df_source0[['user_id', 'gender']], on="user_id", how="inner")

# Now group by title and gender, calculate average rating
grouped = df_full.groupby(['title', 'gender'], as_index=False)['rating'].mean()

# Pivot the table to have columns 'F' and 'M' for average ratings by gender
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating')

# Rename columns to match target schema: 'F' and 'M'
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Reset index to have 'title' as a column
pivot.reset_index(inplace=True)

# Ensure columns order and types as per target schema: ['title': string, 'F': float, 'M': float]
pivot = pivot[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource.csv"
pivot.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on user_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating by title and gender
# Pivot the data to get average rating per gender per title
pivot = (
    joined_all.groupby(["title", "gender"])["rating"]
    .mean()
    .unstack()
    .reset_index()
)

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M", "title": "title"})

# Ensure columns F and M exist even if some gender is missing
if "F" not in pivot.columns:
    pivot["F"] = pd.NA
if "M" not in pivot.columns:
    pivot["M"] = pd.NA

# Reorder columns exactly as target schema
pivot = pivot[["title", "F", "M"]]

# Write output
pivot.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
